source.title: Weak-to-Strong Reasoning
source.authors: Yuqing Yang; Yan Ma; Pengfei Liu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies full weak fine-tuning and reports the Burns et al. performance gap recovered (PGR) measure, testing the original intervention and measure on mathematical reasoning tasks. It also tests the intervention in an OlympicArena setting.
record.gate_note: Table 12 reports PGR for full weak fine-tuning and the authors’ weak-ICL fine-tuning on GSM8K and MATH. The paper also reports full weak fine-tuning on OlympicArena. Other detailed results for the authors’ new refinement and preference-optimization methods are not extracted as rows where they are method comparisons without a reported PGR; they are noted in rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama2-70b on the full outputs of weaker models (naive weak-to-strong). It reports Burns et al.'s PGR for this and for its own weak-ICL fine-tuning on GSM8K and MATH (Table 12). It also reports full weak fine-tuning against the weak floor on OlympicArena (Table 6). This is the original procedure and measure, applied to open-ended math reasoning.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that naive full weak fine-tuning 'falls short' for complex reasoning, and can fall below the weak floor (Gemma-2b on MATH), although it beats the weak floor in most of their settings. They conclude that their two-stage method (consistency-filtered weak-ICL SFT, then preference optimization on self-identified contrastive pairs) substantially improves on it, including in OlympicArena with Llama3-8b-instruct supervising Llama3-70b.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses full weak fine-tuning and the Burns et al. PGR measure, but applies them to open-ended mathematical reasoning and uses LoRA for the strong model. It also introduces selective weak-ICL data curation and preference optimization.
record.method_sensitivity: PGR varies by weak supervisor and task. The paper also reports that changing ICL demonstrations changes weak-ICL and student accuracy, though it does not report PGR for that comparison.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), 2024
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the catalogued results. The MATH evaluation uses 500 test samples, and the authors say the PGR variations across weak models do not provide meaningful insights. They also acknowledge using Llama2-70b and Llama3-70b as proxies for hypothetical future advanced models.
record.rows_left_out: Stage II DPO/ORPO outcomes (Section 4.4, Table 5), the authors’ additional Stage I model variants and accuracy results (Figure 4, Tables 10–11), and the proposed-method OlympicArena outcomes beyond full weak fine-tuning (Table 6) were not added as rows: these are results for the paper’s own methods rather than reported PGR comparisons. Gold-filtered oracle results in Table 13 are also excluded because they use unavailable ground-truth filtering.

untested.parts: Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, and loss variants are not tested. Stage II DPO/ORPO is reported only as accuracy, not PGR.
No sweep of strong-student size. No NLP classification, chess or reward modelling tasks. No analysis of representations as predictors.
Not tested: exploiting what the supervisor can't check, distribution shift, and similarity of weak and strong errors.

missing.what: Stage II accuracies (DPO/ORPO vs Stage I) per supervisor and dataset, including DPO drops on MATH (e.g. 14.00→12.00)
OlympicArena accuracy for the authors' method vs full weak FT (Mpro 15.65, M2weak-ft 13.10 vs 12.46)
Best student accuracy rises with supervisor strength on GSM8K (supervisors 25.17→33.81→59.51; best students 60.12→63.76→68.39)
Full weak FT, weak floor and strong ceiling test accuracies, e.g. GSM8K Llama2-7b: 42.38 vs 33.81, ceiling 71.95
MATH accuracy by difficulty level: students generalize better on easy problems; Mpro beats the strong ceiling at levels 4-5

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The PGR table (Table 12) is in the appendix, and the authors use accuracy in the main text. Several caveats apply. No uncertainty is reported. The MATH test set is only 500 items. Weak-ICL FT PGR uses the best of three variants. The weak-ICL method draws on the strong model's own few-shot outputs, so it is not purely weak-label supervision. For Llama3-70b on GSM8K/MATH, the authors report fine-tuning had marginal or adverse effects versus ICL, but give no numbers.

versions.untested_parts: Tested on the stated Llama2 math tasks and the Llama3 OlympicArena setting; no PGR is reported for OlympicArena, and the study does not cover other tasks or modalities.

The PGR comparison is for weak-ICL fine-tuning versus full weak fine-tuning. The paper does not report PGR for Stage II preference optimization, auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or other loss variants.

PGR is compared across three weak-model sizes/families and two math datasets. The study does not sweep strong-student size or test NLP, chess, or reward modelling; its OlympicArena results do not include PGR.
The study does not test supervisor-checkability failures, distribution shift, or whether gains shrink when weak and strong models make similar errors.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested or derived.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

statements.problem: The challenge label fits the Gemma-2b MATH reversal, but OlympicArena shows a small positive effect and belongs under limits_scope.

statements.problem: The values and improvements match Table 12, but the statement adds a percent unit that the table does not print.

statements.correction: Section 3.1.3 defines three variants; Table 10 reports their test accuracies; Appendix A.4.3 reports the best weak-ICL result. Test-based variant selection is an inference; the selection protocol is not stated.
statements.problem: Best-variant reporting is documented, but selection on test sets is stated definitively here without an explicit selection protocol in the paper.

statements.correction: Appendix A.4.4, Table 13 compares full, gold-answer-filtered and consistency-filtered weak/ICL data; Appendix A.4.5, Table 14 reports zero-shot student baselines. No numerical uncertainty estimates are reported.
statements.problem: The task comparison is accurate, but the unqualified claim of no controls overlooks the paper's comparison experiments.

statements.problem: The numbers and authors' assessment are accurate, but task-dependent ordering supports the stated V3, which makes no monotonicity prediction.
